USER REQUEST
Can you recommend some books written by Frederick Rolfe and Frederick Baron Corvo?

mixtral:8x7b.title: The Desire and Pursuit of the Whole
mixtral:8x7b.explanation: A novel about the life of a Venetian priest, written by Frederick Rolfe.

mixtral:8x7b.title: Hadrian Vii
mixtral:8x7b.explanation: In this provocative novel by Frederick Rolfe, also known as Baron Corvo, a controversial figure rises to the papacy, exploring themes of power, ambition, and the complexities of faith. The story delves into the intricacies of religious politics and personal identity, offering a unique perspective on the nature of leadership.

mixtral:8x7b.title: Hadrian the Seventh
mixtral:8x7b.explanation: A novel about a man unexpectedly becoming Pope, written by Frederick Rolfe, also known as Baron Corvo.

gemma2:9b.title: Hadrian VII
gemma2:9b.explanation: A satirical novel set in an alternate Rome, featuring a fictional emperor.

gemma2:9b.title: Hadrian the Seventh
gemma2:9b.explanation: In this novel by Frederick Rolfe, also known as Baron Corvo, a man unexpectedly becomes Pope and navigates the complexities of faith, power, and personal ambition. The story delves into themes of identity and the human condition, all wrapped in Rolfe's unique narrative style.

gemma2:9b.title: Chou-Chou: A Novel.
gemma2:9b.explanation: An experimental work blending fantasy and autobiography.
